newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan will not intervene in island dispute - minister.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan will not intervene in island dispute - minister.

text.p: Taiwan will not intervene militarily in a dispute over a group of East China Sea islands that are subject to rival territorial claims from China, Japan and Taiwan, Taipei's defence minister said on Wednesday.

Hong Kong Cable Television news quoted Defence Minister Chiang Chung-ling as saying Taiwan's armed forces would not directly intervene in the islands, which China calls the Diaoyus and Japan calls the Senkakus.

Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China. Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
But Chiang said his forces were prepared for emergencies.

Chiang said he would not send forces to protect the Kien Hwa 2, a protest ship from Hong Kong that was heading to the islands on Wednesday, if it ran into trouble with the Japanese because the ship was flying the flag of mainland China, not Taiwan.
A senior Taiwan Navy officer confirmed during the television broadcast that the navy was holding annual firing exercises in the eastern strait.

There had been confusion on Tuesday when the protest ship's captain said he had received a message that Japan was planning live-fire naval drills near the islands. He had apparently confused Japan with Taiwan.
Last Saturday, Taiwan Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng told a parliamentary committee that Taiwan was prepared to defend the islands -- but only as a last resort.
